title: Module quiz: Stakeholders and the project lifecycle

questions.stem: Scenario: Noor tells a sponsor that an assistant is "98 percent accurate overall". The system answers three kinds of dispute, and the one that costs 250 per error is right 63 times in 100. What should the record say to the sponsor?

options.text: That the costly kind is excluded from the figure because it is handled in another system
options.says: Ruled out because the page says to "Promise what you measure and measure what you promise", and excluding a segment breaks both.

options.text: That the overall figure stands, since the costly kind is a small share of the traffic
options.says: Ruled out because "an average hides the segments that cost the most", whatever the traffic share.

options.text: That a person decides each of those until the measured result improves
options.says: The promise is made per segment, and a person decides the costly one.

options.text: That the figure will be re-measured once per quarter, with the same overall method
options.says: Ruled out because "a promise is made once and kept for as long as the system runs", so re-measuring the same overall figure repeats the same blind spot.

questions.stem: Scenario: Lars hands a finished assistant to an operations team with an architecture diagram and a list of settings. The first alert fires on a Saturday and nobody knows who should act on it. Which part of the hand-off was missing?

options.text: A longer pilot, so that more alerts would have fired before the launch
options.says: Ruled out because "a diagram without the runbook leaves the first incident to the person who happens to remember", and a longer pilot adds no owner.

options.text: A named owner for the service and a runbook that tells staff what to do
options.says: The record names an owner and a runbook for each alert.

options.text: A monthly report to the sponsor listing the alerts of the previous period
options.says: Ruled out because "The people who run the system are not the people who built it", and a report to the sponsor does not reach them on a Saturday.

options.text: A second diagram showing the alert thresholds drawn on the architecture
options.says: Ruled out because "Implementation guidance is part of the hand-off and not an extra", and a second diagram adds none.

questions.stem: Scenario: A reviewer corrects forty answers in a week, and the notes of the sponsor review record them. Nothing else changes, and the same errors appear the next week. Which step would have closed the loop?

options.text: Sending the notes to the engineers with a request to read them before the next release
options.says: Ruled out because a loop closes only when "the person who raised the problem is told what happened" after a change has gone through the gate.

options.text: Asking the reviewers to correct the same answers a second time for the record
options.says: Ruled out because "A stakeholder review that produces notes and no cases has not closed anything".

options.text: Moving the review from weekly to daily so that the notes are fresher
options.says: Ruled out because the review is "A regular review of the segments, the saving and the open risks", and its speed adds no case.

options.text: Turning each fix into a labelled evaluation case that each later release is run against
options.says: A loop is closed when a change goes back out through the gate.
